AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Food Nutrients.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Nutrients.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Nutrients.

2. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

3. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food Frying Frying? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food Frying Frying.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preservation of Cereals and Pulses? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Uses of Domestic Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Preservation of Cereals and Pulses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients.

2. A — Ice melting to water

3. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

4. D — newton (N)

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.

6. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

8. D — Producers
